title: docker e2e harness depends on a live public npm install, so a required check is non-deterministic
description:
Filed by the opum-agent orchestrator session from CI evidence.

`docker e2e harness (real lore + backlog binaries)` failed on PR #544 with 375
assertions passing and 3 failing. The three are one root cause, not three defects:

  [FAIL] docusaurus npm install (real)      exit 1,   expected 0
  [FAIL] docusaurus npm run build (real)    exit 127, expected 0
  [FAIL] docusaurus produced build/index.html

Exit 127 is "command not found" -- the build could not run because the install that
should have provided the binary had already failed. The install ran for 28 seconds
(22:19:39 -> 22:20:07) before giving up. `lore scaffold docusaurus` PASSED
immediately before it, so lore's own behavior was correct; only the third-party
dependency fetch failed. The mkdocs pair, which does not npm-install, passed.

Transient, established rather than assumed: the identical content passed this exact
check on PR #543 minutes earlier, the change under test was a `.quest/tasks/*.json`
record which cannot reach a docusaurus install, and re-running the SAME job on the
SAME commit returned success.

THE DEFECT IS NOT THE FLAKE, IT IS THE DEPENDENCY.

This step performs a live `npm install` against the public registry from inside a
container, and it is one of the three checks REQUIRED on `dev` -- the ref this
repository gates, unlike the rest of the fleet. So the gate on every landing here
is coupled to npm registry availability. Three consequences, in increasing order of
cost:

1. Landing is blocked by an outage nobody in this repository caused.
2. Every such failure is indistinguishable from a real regression until someone
   reads 378 assertion lines to find that the 3 reds share one external cause.
3. The cheap response -- re-run until green -- becomes habit, and habitual re-running
   is exactly how a genuine failure gets waved through. This is the second flaky
   required check found in this repository within one hour; see LCLI-429, a webkit
   timing race in the explorer qualification. Two independent sources of
   nondeterminism in front of a blocking ruleset is a pattern, not bad luck.

Suggested directions, cheapest first:
- Pin and vendor the docusaurus dependency set into the image, so the harness tests
  lore's scaffold output rather than the registry's uptime.
- Failing that, retry the install with backoff INSIDE the step and report the
  retries, so a network fault is visibly a network fault rather than a red check.
- Capture npm's stderr into the harness output. The harness currently prints only
  `[FAIL] docusaurus npm install (real) (exit 1, expected 0)`, which is why
  diagnosing this needed the raw run log. A failure that does not say why costs the
  next reader the same twenty minutes.

Do NOT fix this by removing the assertion. Verifying that a scaffolded site really
builds is the point of a "real binaries" harness.

Run: https://github.com/opum-ai/lore-cli/actions/runs/33812287851

acceptanceCriteria.text: The docker e2e harness does not fetch third-party packages from a live public registry during a required check
A failing install reports the underlying npm error in the harness output, not just an exit code
The scaffolded-site build assertion is retained

plan: 1. Dockerfile: pre-warm an offline npm cache at image build time by running the REAL compiled lore binary's `lore scaffold docusaurus` in a scratch dir, then `npm install --cache /opt/npm-cache` there -- extracts the real, pinned package.json rather than duplicating version numbers.

2. run-e2e.sh Phase 19: change the runtime `npm install` to `npm install --offline --cache /opt/npm-cache` so the required check never touches the live registry; keep npm run build + the build/index.html assertion unchanged (AC3).

3. lib/steps.sh: on FAIL, step()/step_json()/step_fail() print a tail of captured stderr to the CI log (not just exit code) -- generalizes the fix past just the install step, matches selftest.sh (stdout/stderr-redirecting expect()) so it stays safe.
4. Verify Dockerfile syntax and shellcheck run-e2e.sh/steps.sh locally (no Docker daemon available in this sandbox); real validation happens on the PR's docker-e2e required check.
